items.stem: Several senior stakeholders each insist their feature goes first. The Product Owner should order the Product Backlog primarily by:

options.text: Value, risk and dependencies toward the product goal
options.rationale: Correct: the PO orders the backlog to maximise value, not by seniority.

options.text: Whichever stakeholder has the highest title

options.rationale: Arrival order does not reflect value.

items.explanation: Correct: the PO orders the backlog to maximise value, not by seniority.

items.stem: A Product Owner says value can only be delivered when the whole project is finished. This view conflicts with Scrum because Scrum aims to:

options.text: Deliver a valuable, usable Increment at least every Sprint
options.rationale: Correct: Scrum delivers value incrementally, not only at the end.

options.text: Avoid delivering anything until the end
Release only once per year by rule
options.rationale: Scrum sets no such annual rule.

items.explanation: Correct: Scrum delivers value incrementally, not only at the end.

items.stem: Which TWO are genuine accountabilities of the Product Owner? (Select TWO)

options.text: Ordering the Product Backlog to maximise value
options.rationale: Correct: the PO orders the backlog.
Correct: the PO ensures the backlog is clear and transparent.
Developers build the product, not the PO.
That is not a Scrum accountability.

options.text: Approving every line of the Definition of Done alone
options.rationale: The Definition of Done is owned by the Scrum Team, not the PO alone.

items.explanation: Correct: the PO orders the backlog. Correct: the PO ensures the backlog is clear and transparent.
